# Tasks demo README: how to run the demo yourself
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #158, sha256:aaec37e9e626415969cf907c6f1351d050fb49022cba96e2ce8a319b086f6107). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Done 2026-10-28 (README with exact steps and a drift test; CI green on f1a0284; Decider D106)
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** docs (small card; a README plus a test that keeps it true)
- **Milestone:** Usable v1 (shortest path to a real prototype)
- **Source:** Found 2026-10-28 after the milestone was reached: the Usable v1 report tells the reader to see the demo README, but demo/tasks has none. The steps were run by hand once (compile, build, specs, start, curl) and worked.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Story:** As Steve, I want a README next to the Tasks demo that gives the exact commands to compile it from Phrase to C#, build it, run its specs, start it and call an endpoint, with the output to expect at each step, so that I can run the demo myself without asking the mob.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given demo/tasks/README.md, When it is read, Then it lists the prerequisites (the .NET 8 SDK), the five commands (phrase build to an output folder, dotnet build of Tasks.Api, dotnet test of Tasks.Specs, dotnet run of Tasks.Api on a fixed local port, and curl calls for create, list with available=true, complete, get, delete and one failure) with the expected output of each, and says the data is in memory and that failures answer 422 with a declared error name
  2. Given a test, When it runs, Then it extracts the fenced commands from the README and checks that every file, project name, route and request field it mentions exists in demo/tasks/Tasks.phrase or the generated output, so the README cannot drift from the app
  3. Given scripts/usable-v1-report.py, When it prints the milestone line, Then the README path it points to exists

## Context

- Output folder in the README should be outside the repo or git-ignored. The list endpoint takes an available flag only so a spec can reach its storage-failure path; say so in one sentence.
